title: Real-Time Agent Coaching: Closing the Feedback Loop
summary: Help support agents improve with immediate feedback after AI training Simulations, clear Scorecards, and focused repeat practice.
body_markdown:
Feedback is easier to apply when the Learner can remember the decision that prompted it. In support training, coaching immediately after a practice conversation lets agents review what happened, understand a missed step, and try a different response.


This guide focuses on immediate feedback during training.[Solidroad](https://www.solidroad.com/) gives Learners personalized coaching after AI customer Simulations, so they can work on a skill before handling the situation with a customer.


## Why feedback timing matters


When coaching arrives long after an exercise, Learners may struggle to recall why they chose a response. They can remember the score while losing the context that would help them improve.


Shortening the gap between practice and feedback makes the next step clearer. For example, a Learner who proposed a refund too early can review which questions they missed and repeat the exercise with a better understanding of the customer's problem.


Feedback should be specific enough to use. Explain the behavior that met the standard, the part that needs work, and what the Learner can try in the next attempt.


## Different ways to deliver coaching


### Trainer-led practice


A Trainer can observe a role-play, pause the exercise, or discuss it afterward. This gives Learners a chance to ask questions and work through difficult judgments. It also requires time from both the Trainer and the Learner.


Reserve that time for situations where discussion adds value: interpreting a policy, handling a sensitive conversation, or helping someone who has repeated an exercise without making progress.


### Feedback after AI Simulations


In Solidroad, Trainers build Simulations with AI customers and attach Scorecards based on the team's standards. Learners complete the conversation and receive feedback after each attempt.


This gives Learners opportunities to practice independently. A manager can review their results and decide who needs another Assignment or a coaching conversation.


### Practice that includes the software workflow


A good customer response may still lead to an incorrect outcome if the agent enters the wrong data or misses a process step. System simulations let Learners practice the software workflow alongside the conversation.


Review both parts of the attempt. The Learner should understand whether the problem was an explanation, a decision, a missed field, or an incorrect action in the system.


## Build a feedback cycle Learners can follow


Use the[SCORE methodology](https://www.solidroad.com/resources/solidroad-score-methodology-systematic-agent-development-through-ai-simulation) to give practice a clear structure:


1. Set the customer situation and the expected outcome.
2. Let the Learner complete the conversation and any workflow steps.
3. Review the Scorecard and coaching together.
4. Choose a specific improvement for the next attempt.
5. Repeat with a variation to check whether the skill carries over.


Keep the practice focused. An agent working on explaining a cancellation policy needs a scenario that exercises that skill, with feedback that refers to what they said and did.


## Make room for practice in the working week


Independent Simulations can reduce the scheduling needed for routine practice. Managers still need time to choose useful Assignments, review results, and support Learners who need help.


Start by measuring the time Trainers spend preparing, delivering, and following up on an exercise. During a pilot, compare that workload with the time needed to configure a Simulation, review its feedback, and coach exceptions. Use your team's results to estimate capacity.


Give agents a defined period for practice. Adding Assignments without time to complete them makes training compete with customer work and makes progress harder to interpret.


## Common implementation problems


### Feedback is too broad


Comments such as "show more empathy" leave the Learner to decide what that means. Tie coaching to a moment in the conversation and an action they can repeat, such as acknowledging the customer's frustration before explaining the policy.


### Scenarios do not resemble the job


Review scenarios with experienced agents. Check the customer context, policy details, and workflow against the situations new hires will encounter. Adjust the difficulty as Learners become more confident.


### Learners do not understand the scores


Explain the Scorecard before practice. Trainers should review sample attempts and calibrate scoring against their expectations. Give Learners a way to raise questions about feedback that seems unclear or inconsistent.


## Measure whether coaching helps


Track the time from an identified skill need to demonstrated proficiency, results across repeated attempts, and performance on unfamiliar variations. Managers can also record which Learners need additional support.


Use existing customer reporting to assess how skills transfer to work. Customer satisfaction and handling time can provide context, but changes in staffing, workload, and case complexity also affect them.
